Slide 1 covers Mohammad Hatta (Bung Hatta), who resigned on 1 December 1956 due to political differences with President Sukarno over Guided Democracy. Slide 2 covers B.J. summary: A male presenter in a batik shirt explains breaking news that Indonesia's Vice President Gibran has resigned. He shows clips and headlines stating the resignation was accepted by President Prabowo, who greeted him warmly, and that the DPR subsequently canceled its plenary session on impeachment. Photos of Gibran being removed from walls illustrate that Indonesia temporarily has no vice president. The presenter notes Gibran returns to civilian life, joking he's now like everyone else, referencing a meme about unemployment rising to 19,000,001. He details Gibran's lifetime benefits under Law No. 7/1978: about Rp23.27 million per month pension plus wife/child/rice allowances, plus non-cash facilities like an official house, car, driver, VVIP health insurance, and Paspampres security. For the country, he cites MPR Chairman Ahmad Muzani confirming the vacancy, and explains the constitutional process: the President proposes two names to the MPR, which must elect a replacement within 60 days per Article 8(2) of the 1945 Constitution. Who will replace him is still unknown. The presenter then links this to other high-profile departures on the same day: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigning after leading the company since 1993 amid a scandal, and Manchester United coach Michael Carrick being sacked for poor performance. He ends by asking viewers for their opinion on the sudden wave of resignations.

There is significant distrust toward DPR/MPR, accusations of political maneuvering, and calls to check officials' diplomas. Sentiment is largely negative toward elites, mixed toward Gibran personally, with some sympathy and many jokes. Users ask who will replace him, speculate names like Teddy, Hashim, or Puan, and lament the lack of a VP and First Lady. The tone is informal, sarcastic, and politically charged. 1. **Criticism of Gibran receiving pension despite short tenure:** "Enak bener ya jadi Gibran. Jadi pengangguran juga, tapi malah dapat tunjangan dari APBN" 2. **Jokes about Gibran playing GTA 6 after resigning:** "Mas Gibran mau fokus main GTA 6" 3. **Debate over replacement candidates:** "Siapa yang akan gantiin beliau? focus: Reactions to Gibran's resignation, his lifetime benefits, and who should replace him.

Slides 1-2 outline the petition filed September 10th by former Deputy Minister Denny Indrayana challenging KPU's rule change allowing foreign diplomas, and provide Gibran's education timeline (Singapore secondary school, UTS Insearch college prep in Australia 2004-2007, MDIS bachelor's 2007-2010), noting he never attended an Indonesian SMA/SMK. Slides 3-5 detail the core issue: the 2019 'surat keterangan' stating his Year 12 coursework was equivalent to SMK knowledge but was not an official equivalency certificate, and was issued based only on attendance transcripts. Petitioners argued KPU's 2024 regulation (PKPU No. 19/2023) waiving high school proof for candidates with university degrees was manipulative and violated the Election Law requiring senior secondary completion. Slides 6-7 state the petitioners sought disqualification and new elections, but MK dismissed the case on October 6th because petitioners lacked legal standing as non-contestants, while acknowledging MK never found conclusive proof of a foreign high school diploma—only a certificate of attendance. Slide 8 concludes the case is closed but legitimacy issues remain, citing scholars who say responsibility shifts to DPR for impeachment, police for investigation, and KPU accountability, and that the unresolved diploma could bar Gibran from running in 2029.
